text: Business logic vulnerabilities (or logic flaws) are design and implementation defects that allow attackers to manipulate legitimate application workflows to elicit unintended behavior. These flaws emerge when developers fail to anticipate unusual application states or enforce business constraints server-side, enabling attackers to bypass purchase workflows, alter transaction-critical variables, or submit out-of-order requests without triggering traditional web vulnerability signatures.

metadata.title: Business Logic Vulnerabilities Core Concept
root_causes: Flawed developer assumptions about user behavior
Failure to anticipate unusual server states
Absence of server-side state and invariant verification
metadata.detection_profile: Low signature detectability; requires domain understanding and context-aware state analysis.

text: Root causes of business logic flaws: 1) Client-side trust bias: assuming traffic originates solely from conforming browser interfaces, leading to weak or absent server-side validation. 2) Inter-component integration assumptions: in complex architectures, engineers make unvalidated assumptions about how auxiliary modules process and sanitize state. 3) Undocumented implicit assumptions: state transitions and precondition constraints are rarely formalized, leaving state machines susceptible to step-skipping and arbitrary transitions via proxy interception.

metadata.title: Root Causes and Mechanism of Logic Flaws
attack_vectors: Direct endpoint invocation bypassing client checks
prerequisites: Application dependence on implicit state sequencing

text: Excessive trust in client-side controls occurs when server-side logic assumes incoming requests originate solely from a conforming browser interface, neglecting server-side validation and integrity verification. Attackers intercept requests via local proxies (e.g., Burp Proxy) to tamper with transaction-critical parameters like price, role, or user ID before processing.

metadata.title: Excessive Trust in Client-Side Controls
metadata.vulnerability_class: CWE-602: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security
metadata.flawed_assumption: User input arriving at the backend has already satisfied client-side validation rules.
metadata.impact: Arbitrary parameter tampering, transaction value manipulation, and authorization bypass.

text: Failing to handle unconventional input in numeric fields allows attackers to bypass business invariants and reverse transactional flows. For example, in a fund transfer verification where `transferAmount <= currentBalance`, passing a negative integer (e.g., -1000) evaluates to true and causes balance deductions to function as additions, transferring funds from the recipient to the sender.

metadata.title: Numeric Sign Error and Unconventional Input Handling
metadata.attack_mechanism: Supplying unexpected negative numbers, extreme values, or mismatched types to exploit incomplete server-side domain constraints.

text: Inconsistent security controls arise from the assumption that a user or dataset remains trustworthy indefinitely once initial validation checks pass. Relaxing security checks in downstream components or later workflow steps creates loopholes where authenticated users can invoke operations without ongoing privilege verification.

metadata.title: Assumption of Persistent User Trustworthiness
metadata.flawed_assumption: A user authenticated at step 1 remains authorized and compliant across subsequent operations without continuous re-validation.

text: An encryption oracle vulnerability occurs when an application encrypts arbitrary user-supplied input and returns the resulting ciphertext to the user. An attacker leverages this oracle to construct valid encrypted payloads using the application's internal key and cipher, feeding the forged ciphertext into sensitive endpoints that trust encrypted data without verifying its origin or integrity.

metadata.title: Authentication Bypass via Encryption Oracle
metadata.exploit_path: Arbitrary text -> Oracle Encryption -> Valid Ciphertext Generation -> Injected into Authorization Cookie/Token
compounding_factors: Co-existence of decryption oracle allowing plaintext recovery
Shared key usage between low-privilege input handling and high-privilege access tokens

text: Email address parser discrepancies emerge when different components of an application (e.g., web entry validation, domain routing, and authentication backends) parse RFC-compliant or obfuscated email formats inconsistently. By applying specific encodings or syntax variations, attackers bypass domain-matching rules to register unauthorized accounts for restricted internal domains.

metadata.title: Access Control Bypass via Email Parser Discrepancies
metadata.impact: Unauthorized access to tenant data, internal admin privileges, and organization domain bypass.
